Urban II’s description of Jerusalem as “the navel of the world” and a place “consecrated by suffering” and “glorified by burial” emphasizes its spiritual importance to Christians. The speech urges listeners to liberate Jerusalem from non-Christian control so that holy sites can be accessed and honored properly. This fits within the broader medieval practice of pilgrimage to sacred sites, which was a major feature of Christian devotional life, and the call to free Jerusalem would resonate with those who valued such pilgrimages.
